summary: This resolution recognizes the 1885 Rock Springs Chinese Massacre by honoring the at least 28 murdered Chinese miners, condemning the mob violence and official inaction, and directing education, historical research, and site commemoration efforts to address anti-Asian discrimination.

scores.thoughts: The resolution contains no provisions, authorizations, or references related to federal spending, appropriations, or budgets of any kind. It is a purely symbolic recognition measure.
No content addresses tax policy, rates, credits, or revenue measures.
The bill has no connection to healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
No references to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

The resolution explicitly discusses Chinese immigrant laborers, the Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882, anti-immigrant violence, and the need to acknowledge immigrant contributions while working toward racial justice. This symbolically supports a more inclusive view of immigration history and protections, creating a minor negative tilt on the scale.
No relation to reproductive rights or abortion policy.
No provisions or mentions concerning military or defense spending.
Mentions historic preservation programs but does not engage environmental regulations or climate policy.
No content related to welfare programs or social safety net policies.

Paragraphs (6) and (8) encourage education about the massacre in schools and higher education institutions. This has a tangential connection to public education content but does not address funding, investment levels, or school choice.
No references to drugs, enforcement, or decriminalization.

The text condemns the historical failure of law enforcement to protect victims or hold perpetrators accountable. This touches lightly on accountability themes but proposes no policy changes to criminal justice systems.
No engagement with trade, tariffs, or globalization.
No fiscal or debt-related provisions.
No content concerning LGBTQ+ rights or protections.
No references to foreign aid.
No provisions related to voting access or election integrity.
No technology, data, or privacy provisions.

The resolution describes exploitative labor conditions, lower wages for Chinese workers, and their systematic exclusion from labor unions. This provides minor symbolic recognition of labor exploitation issues but does not alter union policy.
The bill addresses racial discrimination and violence but contains no religious liberty or exemption provisions.
